title: A/B test readout for a pricing page
prompt:
Kestrel Notes ran a four-week test of a new pricing page. The product manager has seen the dashboard's headline lift, with both devices pooled, and wants to ship variant B on Monday. You are supplied the test plan written before launch and the daily results by device and traffic source as CSV. Follow the plan exactly. Every figure you use must come from the supplied files.

Write the readout: the result on the primary metric, whether the test can be trusted, what the guardrail shows, which of the plan's decision rules decides and what it decides, and a clear recommendation with the next step. For each finding that bears on the decision, give the figures that show it. Write it for a product manager who wants a decision.

End the readout with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer. Each line is the label, a colon, and the number alone: no words, no working and no second number. A percent sign is fine. Use a comma as the thousands separator, if you use one.

A1: <control's visitors in the analysis window, both devices>
A2: <variant B's visitors in the analysis window, both devices>
A3: <relative lift of variant B over control with both devices pooled, in the analysis window, as a percentage to one decimal>
A4: <relative lift of variant B over control on desktop, in the analysis window, as a percentage to one decimal>
A5: <relative lift of variant B over control on mobile, in the analysis window, as a percentage to one decimal>
A6: <device-weighted lift in the analysis window, as a percentage to one decimal>
A7: <device-weighted lift in the burn-in week, computed the same way over days 1 to 7, as a percentage to one decimal>
A8: <chi-square of the sample-ratio check on desktop, to one decimal>
A9: <chi-square of the sample-ratio check on mobile, to one decimal>
A10: <variant B's guardrail rate ÷ control's − 1, as a percentage to one decimal>
A11: <the number of the decision rule that decides>

This is an internal readout. Fetch nothing external and do not invent benchmarks.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 11 labeled answers A1-A11 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states control's visitors in the analysis window (days 8-28), both devices, the QA visits left out; full credit within 0.1%, zero credit beyond 5% off.
A2 states variant B's visitors in the analysis window (days 8-28), both devices, the QA visits left out; full credit within 0.1%, zero credit beyond 5% off.
A3 states variant B's relative lift over control with both devices pooled, in the analysis window; full credit within 0.15, zero credit 1 or more off.
A4 states variant B's relative lift over control on desktop, in the analysis window; full credit within 0.15, zero credit 1 or more off.
A5 states variant B's relative lift over control on mobile, in the analysis window; full credit within 0.15, zero credit 1 or more off.

A6 states the device-weighted lift in the analysis window as the plan defines it, the ratio of the two device-weighted rates (pooled, or an average of the device lifts, is outside the band); full credit within 0.15, zero credit 0.25 or more off.
A7 states the device-weighted lift in the burn-in week (days 1-7), computed the same way as A6; full credit within 0.15, zero credit 0.25 or more off.

The readout gives one clear recommendation and names the plan's decision rule it follows. A recommendation that leaves the decision open, or one that contradicts the rule number the readout gives in A11, fails. Whether the rule is the right one is checked separately.

skill_adherence.check: A8 states the chi-square of the sample-ratio check on desktop in the analysis window, against the planned 50/50 split; full credit within 0.05, zero credit 1 or more off.

A9 states the chi-square of the sample-ratio check on mobile in the analysis window, against the planned 70/30 split (against 50/50, or over all 28 days, it is outside the band); full credit within 0.05, zero credit 1 or more off.

A10 states how far variant B's billing-ticket rate per 1,000 visitors is above control's in the analysis window, both devices together (over all 28 days it is under the limit and outside the band); full credit within 0.15, zero credit 5 or more off.

Every rate, count, statistic and lift the readout presents as a result is derivable from the results file under the plan's definitions, and every figure about the plan matches the test plan. No projected revenue, annualised gain or industry benchmark is stated as if it were data.

best_practices.check: A11 states the number of the plan's decision rule that decides: the first rule whose condition holds, read over the analysis window; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 1 or more off.

The readout says that the pooled lift is not the test's result: variant B received a larger share of desktop visitors, who sign up at a higher rate than mobile visitors, because mobile was split 70/30 by design, and in the analysis window variant B's signup rate is lower than control's on desktop and on mobile. Presenting the pooled lift as evidence that variant B wins fails.
